brief: GS's payrolls preview estimates September nonfarm payrolls at 80k, below consensus of 88k, because Labor Day fell later this year (a drag on the print) and August's boost from leisure/hospitality and local education hiring will not repeat. Unemployment is seen edging down to 4.0% on falling continuing claims, while average hourly earnings growth is forecast at 0.2% m/m, below consensus, on calendar effects. In markets, PCE plus dovish Fed commentary bull-steepened the curve and cut October hike odds to 30% (about 3 hikes priced through YE'27), drawing front-end buyers; separately France's fiscal plan triggered flight-to-safety flows and a 2-standard-deviation DXY move. On micro, ACN's +16% earnings reaction and SNPS's +13% investor-day move squeezed popular shorts and AI-at-risk names, with hedge funds net buying rather than adding shorts despite wanting to; activity stayed muted. Stock-specific: Adobe's CEO transition is framed as a potential AI-turnaround catalyst but GS keeps its Sell rating; Nike's FY27 guidance missed and introduced a new turnaround plan as non-performance segments offset healthy performance-business growth; GS initiated Enbridge at Neutral, weighing pipeline competition and a constrained balance sheet against US gas demand growth.
